title: DRC Situation Update: Cases Reach 4,566, Deaths Cross 2,128
detail: The DRC Ministry of Health published a situation update on 12 August 2026 (data as of 11 August) recording 4,566 cumulative confirmed cases and 2,128 cumulative deaths — an increase of 117 confirmed cases and 67 deaths since the 11 August report. 570 patients were hospitalized in isolation, with 53 of 140 affected health zones across five provinces. Reuters wire coverage the same day, citing a new Science journal analysis, described the outbreak as the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record: deaths rose from 1,000 to 2,000 in under a month, versus over 12 months for DRC's 2018–2020 Kivu outbreak and nearly 5 months for the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic to reach 1,000 deaths. Conflict, delayed detection, and strained health services continue to hamper contact tracing, patient isolation, and transmission control.

sources.name: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC)

title: WHO and DRC Advance Talks to Launch Phase 3 Ervebo Trial Against Bundibugyo
detail: STAT News reported on 12 August 2026 that WHO and DRC authorities are advancing talks to launch a Phase 3 clinical trial testing whether vaccines can help contain the Bundibugyo outbreak, following WHO's 7 August recommendation. Merck's Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) — licensed for Zaire ebolavirus, with roughly 84% effectiveness against that species in prior field studies and a roughly 500,000-dose stockpile available — would be the first candidate, with the trial design randomizing individual contacts of cases to vaccine or placebo. Bundibugyo-specific candidates from Oxford Vaccine Group, Moderna, and IAVI may be added later. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said: 'It's already the second-biggest Ebola epidemic on record, and it's moving faster than any previous Ebola outbreak.'
